AUTHOR: Tödtmann
TITLE: Time-unfolding Object Existence Detection in Low-quality Underwater Videos using Convolutional Neural Networks
VENUE: PROCEEDINGS OF THE 15TH INTERNATIONAL JOINT CONFERENCE ON COMPUTER VISION, IMAGING AND COMPUTER GRAPHICS THEORY AND APPLICATIONS, VOL 5: VISAPP
REGION: Eight rivers, Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania (Baltic catchments), Germany
SPECIES: Sea trout (Salmo trutta) presence/absence per video
DATA: Own motion-triggered river camera videos (341,238 videos, 8 rivers, 5 months); ~10% manually labelled
V_EV: Sec. 6 Conclusion: 'The approach detects objects in underwater videos even in use cases with reduced quality: low resolution, minimal contrast, poor visibility.'
D2: 10% of videos labelled; 50% train / 50% val+test; headline test on 6,000-video sample of 307,114 unlabelled (unseen) videos
D_EV: Sec. 5: 'The trained network has been evaluated with unlabeled videos... comprehends 307 114 unlabeled videos'; Table 1 'previously unseen' data; each video is one grid-image sample.
R_EV: Sec. 5: test videos are the remaining unlabelled videos of the same campaign: 'a showcase sample of 6 000 videos from the 307 114 videos has been selected'
C_EV: Sec. 5: 'A manual control by the domain expert Uwe Friedrich confirmed that 5 098 of 5 235 videos were containing sea trout, resulting in a precision of 97.38%.'
E_EV: Sec. 5/Table 2: only precision/accuracy of video classification reported: 'an accuracy of 97.70 % is achieved'
ARCH: Modified GoogLeNet on 8x8 time-unfolded frame grids (Caffe/DIGITS)
NOTE: Each video = one grid image, so split is at video level, but the 50/50 split is not described as grouped/random and class balancing by duplication was applied (possible duplicate leakage within the labelled train/val split). Headline evaluation is on unlabelled videos not in the labelled 10%. Pretraining source of GoogLeNet not stated. Fixed river cameras at constructed bottlenecks (fishway-like). FN=36 in confusion matrix coded as FNR. Softmax confidence listed in report but no threshold value given.
